_why: Every price the catalog shows comes from this file. One place, so an
estimate can never be half-updated, and so the assumption is reviewable
rather than buried in a template.
THESE ARE NOT QUOTES. They are a published industry band for FDM service
pricing, and nothing here has been checked against a real order. The whole
point of showing an estimate is to tell someone whether a build is a $50
decision or a $400 one before they get invested, and a number that is wrong
by 3x does that worse than no number at all.
To replace them with something real: npm run quote-bundle <slug> makes a zip
a provider's quote page will accept. Put one through, then set `source` and
`calibrated` below to what came back and narrow the band to match.
source: industry band for FDM service pricing
_materials_why: The official packs specify PLA and TPU only. PETG and CF-nylon are priced
here anyway because a contributed pack may name them, and an unpriced
material drops silently out of the estimate rather than announcing itself.

PLA.note: What the packs specify. The cheapest and most widely stocked FDM material; every service and every printer carries it, and it needs no hardened nozzle, dry box or enclosure.

TPU 95A.note: Services quote TPU by shore hardness and the common service grade is 88A, softer than the 95A these packs specify. Treat a TPU quote as a substitution until confirmed.

PETG.note: Not used by the official packs; priced for contributed ones. Note that Protolabs Network stocks PETG in black, grey and white only, so a coloured PETG pack cannot be serviced as drawn.

CF-nylon.note: Not used by the official packs; priced for contributed ones. An industrial-FDM material, not a desktop one, and the single most expensive thing a pack can ask for. Protolabs Network quotes it as Markforged Onyx, a specific product rather than a generic PA-CF.

setup_note: MEASURED, not assumed: a real quote for one 12 cm3 PLA part came back at $40, which at that size is essentially all floor. Was guessed at $25 before that. A floor dominates a small order: it is almost the entire cost of printing one bracket and a small fraction of the cost of a whole body.
_what_the_quote_did_not_tell_us: A 12 cm3 part never clears a $40 minimum, so that quote fixes the intercept
and says nothing about the slope. The per_cm3 figures below are still the
industry band, which is why `calibrated` is still false.
To get the slope, quote something whose volume bill exceeds the floor: at
the high end that is about 100 cm3. Scout's whole PLA set is 111 cm3 and
Rover Lite's is 624 cm3, so a full-body plate answers it.
Still unknown, and it is the difference between a $120 body and a $760 one:
whether that $40 is charged per ORDER or per PART. Quoting two parts at
once settles it - about $40 means per order, about $80 means per part.
_pricing_model: estimate = setup_usd + sum over parts of (volume_cm3 x qty x usd_per_cm3)
Volume is the solid figure from the STL, which is what a service prices on:
they choose their own walls and infill, so the printed mass that matters to
someone running their own printer is not the number a service bills.
